title: a teas table, filled one INSERT at a time, then three kinds of id column

steps.sql:
CREATE TABLE teas (
  id     int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name   text NOT NULL,
  origin text,
  grams  int NOT NULL DEFAULT 100
)
steps.note: a brand new table: four columns, no rows.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: empty. a table is just its columns until something goes in.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO teas (name, origin, grams) VALUES ('assam', 'india', 250)
steps.note: one row. you named three columns; id came from the identity column's sequence.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: the table after it.

steps.sql:
INSERT INTO teas (name, origin) VALUES
  ('sencha', 'japan'),
  ('darjeeling', 'india'),
  ('rooibos', 'south africa')
steps.note: three rows in one statement. nobody said grams, so each got the default, 100.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: the table after it.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO teas (name, origin, grams) VALUES ('house blend', DEFAULT, DEFAULT)
steps.note: DEFAULT asks for the default by name. origin has none, so NULL is its default.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: the table after it.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO teas (origin) VALUES ('china')
steps.note: no name, and name is NOT NULL. the whole statement fails and nothing is written.

error.message: null value in column "name" of relation "teas" violates not-null constraint

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: the table after it: unchanged.

steps.sql: BEGIN
steps.note: a transaction. nothing inside it is real until COMMIT.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO teas (name, origin, grams) VALUES ('pu-erh', 'china', 357)
steps.note: pu-erh goes in, and takes the next id from the sequence.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: inside the transaction, the row is there.

steps.sql: ROLLBACK
steps.note: ROLLBACK. the row goes, but the sequence never gives a number back.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: the table after it.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO teas (name, origin, grams) VALUES ('oolong', 'taiwan', 50)
steps.note: the next insert gets 8. 6 went to the insert that failed, 7 to the one rolled back.

steps.sql: SELECT id, name, origin, grams FROM teas ORDER BY id
steps.note: the table after it: a gap at 6 and 7, for good.
GENERATED ALWAYS: the identity column refuses a value you typed. the mistake is caught on the spot.

error.message: cannot insert a non-DEFAULT value into column "id"
error.detail: Column "id" is an identity column defined as GENERATED ALWAYS.

steps.sql: DROP TABLE kinds
steps.note: clean up for the next kind.
GENERATED BY DEFAULT takes the typed 1. the sequence doesn't know, hands out 1 next, and the second insert hits the primary key.

error.message: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "kinds_pkey"

steps.sql: DROP TABLE kinds
steps.note: clean up for the next kind.
serial does the same: a plain DEFAULT nextval(...), which a typed value simply skips.

error.message: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "kinds_pkey"
